rulings.evidence: REUSE, not a proposal: whole-chicken is a live commodity id at 7 of 7 stores. The missing vocabulary row is a naming question, not a registrar one (brown-lentils precedent). NOT rotisserie-chicken, which is cooked pulled meat, and not any breast row.

No quantity is given by the source, so the 2 tsp salt booked here is MY estimate for a 6 lb bird plus a pan of vegetables, with the matching black pepper on the buy string. Marked optional because the source treats it as season-to-taste.

A bunch and sprigs is unambiguously FRESH thyme; the board's dried-thyme near-miss is a form flip with a different price class and about three times the strength per gram. fresh-thyme is a live id at 4 of 7 stores. Bunch about 25 g plus 20 sprigs at ~1 g each.

lemons is a live each-priced commodity. NOT lemon-juice, which is the bottled form flip and a different price class. House each-weight 100 g for a medium lemon; halved, stuffed and discarded, so its macros are near-immaterial.

rulings.raw: 1 large yellow onion (sliced into large chunks)
rulings.evidence: Exact vocabulary row Yellow Onion [onions], 7 of 7 board. Not red-onion, which is a separate variety price class. House large-onion each-weight 170 g.

rulings.raw: 1 bulb of fennel (tops removed, cut into wedges)
rulings.evidence: Fresh bulb, NOT Ground Fennel seed (form flip, 345 vs 31 cal per 100 g and a spice-jar price class). The fennel commodity's unit is 'each', which is the fresh bulb, matching the existing Fennel Bulb macro row.

Exact vocabulary row; unqualified 'flour' in a butter roux is AP wheat flour, 7 of 7 board. Explicitly NOT the almond flour row, whose notes warn the flour commodity include pattern over-claims the bare term.

macro_cross_check.verdict: PASS AT THE EDGE, flagged twice. Calories agree within 4.2% and protein sits at -14.8%, just inside the 15% tolerance, so the 6 lb portion is right and no line needs re-examining. Both gaps run the same direction and have the same cause: I book the bird on an as-purchased basis with 30% bone removed, while the source appears to count more of the carcass as edible. FLAG 1: at 668 cal the computed figure is 18 cal over the run's 650 ceiling, even though the source's own 641 is inside it - and a roast bird leaves a great deal of rendered fat in the pan that this basis still counts, so the true value is likely at or under the source's. FLAG 2: the whole-chicken yield is a disclosed estimate. Carbohydrate is comfortable at 12 g against a 35 g ceiling.
